newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil foreign reserves at $63 billion - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil foreign reserves at $63 billion - cenbank.

text.p: Brazilian Central Bank Monetary Policy Director Francisco Lopes said Thursday the country's foreign reserves had reached $63 billion.

Lopes also told a Chamber of Deputies committee that he expected the current account in the balance of payments to show a deficit this year of between 4.0 percent and 5.0 percent of gross domestic product.
"Today, we already have, according to the international liquidity concept, foreign reserves of $63 billion," Lopes told the lower house's Economy, Industry and Commerce Committee.
"The current account deficit will probably arrive this year at something like four to five percent of GDP," he said.
But he added: "This is not something that worries us or makes us despair. I'm perfectly convinced that a deficit of this size can be easily financed for some years."
Lopes said the size of foreign reserves, as well as inflows of foreign capital, gave him a "great tranquility."
However, he said the Brazilian government was working to reduce the current account deficit and he was sure a reduction will occur as the trade balance improves.
